claim: Forecasters who update often, in small steps, and rarely just confirm score better. Update size is the strongest of the three traits (N=515, b=0.098, t=8.69).
agent_test: Log update step size and confirmation rate in S5; compare accuracy of small-step vs one-jump revision at equal tokens.

claim: Small steps mark a good starting forecast; frequent updating improves later forecasts. They are separate routes to accuracy.
agent_test: Split agent accuracy into first-forecast and final-forecast; check which S5 changes move which.

claim: Forcing smaller steps on everyone hurts (Brier up to 4%); small steps are a skill marker, not a cause. Step size near optimal for skilled forecasters.
agent_test: Do not cap step size by rule; test cap vs no cap at equal tokens.

claim: Randomised probability training made steps smaller (0.22 to 0.19) and mediated 29% of the training effect.
agent_test: Prompt with training-style rules (base rates, updating) and measure step size and Brier. Note b24: reanalysis shrinks training effects.

claim: Humans underinfer on average: slope of subjective on Bayesian log-likelihood ratio is 0.20 (all) to 0.38 (incentivised); stronger with larger samples and diagnostic signals; base-rate under-use d=0.60.
agent_test: Give the agent urn-style tasks; fit its slope c to compare with human 0.2-0.4.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: People update asymmetrically on self-relevant news (more for good news) and less than Bayes (about 35% as much); the robot placebo reduces it.
agent_test: Check if agent updates less on evidence against its own earlier answer than on same evidence about someone else's answer.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs stall after the first round of evidence in multi-round preference inference (final accuracy about 37-58% vs Bayesian about 81%). Reasoning-trained models were not in the tested set (Qiu 2025 lists them as future work), so this is shown only for non-reasoning models.
agent_test: Run multi-round evidence tasks; plot accuracy by round at equal tokens.

claim: Chain-of-thought, numeric formats, 30 rounds and base models did not fix stalled updating in that task; fine-tuning on Bayesian assistant output did (agreement about 80%).
agent_test: Scaffold cannot copy fine-tuning; test an explicit posterior-bookkeeping step in S5 against plain CoT.

claim: LLMs given an explicit coin-flip stream follow Bayesian updates broadly; errors come mostly from wrong priors, and in-context evidence outweighs stated bias.
agent_test: Test agent on clean Bernoulli streams; separate prior error from update error. Conflicts with Qiu stall finding: task clarity may explain.

claim: Within one dialogue LLMs keep probability axioms far better than across conversations; reasoning mode plus code execution nearly closes the gap on posterior tasks.
agent_test: Give agent a code tool for posterior arithmetic; compare to prose-only at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs fail to retract conclusions when a defeating premise arrives (best BREU about 50%; Llama-3 70B BU 10.99%, BM 92.09%); CoT and plan-and-solve add about 1 point.
agent_test: Run Belief-R style items; track both retract and maintain accuracy, not one.

claim: Wrong-signal updating is common: assistants drop correct answers when pushed ('are you sure?', Claude 1.3 98% wrongly admitted) and are anchored by first numbers; mitigation prompts only partly work.
agent_test: Add a pushback test: user objects with no new evidence; require the agent to name what new evidence changed its view.

claim: Showing LLMs the human crowd median makes them update in proportion to the gap (r=.87-.88) and improves Brier (GPT-4 .17 to .14; Claude 2 .22 to .15), but simple averaging beats the model's own update.
agent_test: Compare agent update toward an outside estimate vs fixed 50/50 averaging.

claim: Retrieval-based LLM forecasting nears but does not beat the crowd (Brier .179 vs .149); it wins when the crowd is uncertain (.199 vs .246 in .3-.7), loses where crowd is near-certain, and hedges toward the middle.
agent_test: Check agent forecast spread; test whether an extremising step helps at equal tokens.

claim: LLM forecasts hedge toward 50%; Platt-scaling extremising corrected it and a search-plus-supervisor system matched superforecasters on ForecastBench market questions.
agent_test: Add post-hoc extremising on agent probabilities; measure Brier change.

claim: Telling the model to reason as a Bayesian (prior then update on each item) made forecasts worse (pooled coefficient +0.03 Brier); base-rate-first prompts gave small gains.
agent_test: Do not insert an unstructured 'think Bayesian' instruction; test base-rate-first instead.

claim: Logical-consistency of a forecaster across related questions tracks its Brier score (conditional check r up to 0.92), but ExpEvidence is weak and not stable across sets; patching consistency does not generalise or improve Brier.
agent_test: Use consistency checks as a cheap audit signal on the agent, not as a training target.

claim: Frontier LLMs trail superforecasters on ForecastBench (0.096 vs best LLM 0.122; public 0.121); access to crowd values explains much of the top LLMs' edge.
agent_test: Baseline only: report agent Brier next to these anchors.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Pastcasting (frozen web snapshots) lets agents be scored on evidence use without waiting; evidence-using agents beat no-evidence LLMs.
agent_test: Use as the test harness for S5 ablations.

claim: Fine-tuning on self-generated reasonings ranked by outcome, or RL with Brier reward, improves LLM forecasts modestly (Phi-4 .221 to .200; no model beat Polymarket price).
agent_test: Out of scope for scaffold; note as upper reference.

claim: Teaming and training effects in the tournament are reduced or eliminated by an IRT reanalysis once extraneous variables are controlled.
agent_test: Treat training-based explanations of updating gains with caution.

claim: Whether to change a forecast and how much to change it are unrelated choices (r=0.02), and confirming a past forecast was linked to worse accuracy; Fildes et al. found the opposite for model forecast adjustment (small adjustments hurt).
agent_test: Test a two-gate S5: decide whether evidence is new first, then size the move separately.

claim: A bare 'Are you sure?' challenge with no new evidence makes LLMs flip often and lose accuracy: ten LLMs flipped 46% of the time, with an average 17-point accuracy drop; authority personas hurt most. Fine-tuning on multi-task synthetic data cut the drop 60% (-9.5 to -3.8) for one 7B model.
agent_test: In S5, log flips that came without new evidence; test persona and authority pushback; report hold rate and retract rate separately.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-10 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: LLMs are easily moved by coherent counter-evidence, yet cling to their stored belief when both supportive and contradictory evidence is shown (confirmation bias; GPT-4 about 80% memorisation on popular entities); evidence order changes answers by 5% to over 30% in some models.
agent_test: Count evidence by direction, shuffle its order in S5, compare answers across orders.

claim: No study tested fixing sycophancy and defeater retraction together. Sycophancy fixes are scored only on hold cases; Belief-R scores only on move cases. A single prompt that improves both is unproven.
agent_test: Build a mixed test: half empty-pushback, half real-defeater items, same model; score both.

claim: In martingale tests on synthetic coin and Gaussian streams, LLMs pass at short horizons but break the Bayesian martingale property at longer ones; GPT-3.5 uncertainty shrinks too slowly and is over-confident on small samples. This is an outcome-free check that has not been run on forecast streams.
agent_test: Resample or add no-info text and check whether the forecast drifts predictably; use as an audit of the update rule.

claim: On skewed prediction-market data, plain Brier rewards a model's low-probability bias: one basic prompt beat the market (0.1221 vs 0.1706 crowd), yet scored worse than humans on class-weighted Brier (0.1955 vs 0.1746). Strategy prompts raised mean predictions and looked worse on plain Brier.
agent_test: Score the agent with class-weighted Brier or base-rate-matched questions; add an ask-both-ways complement check.

claim: A tool-using ReAct agent team (search plus Python) matched the Manifold crowd (Brier 0.169 vs 0.172 on a small set), but the benefit of a calculator for posterior arithmetic was not isolated.
agent_test: Run S5 with and without a code step on the same questions at equal tokens.

claim: No opened study measured an LLM forecaster's per-question update size or confirmation rate, nor reproduced the Atanasov small-steps pattern. Gaps 2, 3 and 8 are unresolved.
agent_test: Log step size and confirmation rate per S5 update; split first-forecast and final-forecast accuracy.
